title: GitLab Examples
description: Small GitLab examples from the lessons. Each example links back to its explanation and practice task.

examples.title: Understand a GitLab project
examples.description: A GitLab project contains a Git repository and related work tools. A group can organise several projects and their access in one place.
examples.code:
Group: school-club
Project: reading-list
Repository: program files and Git history
Related tools: issues, merge requests and pipelines

examples.title: Read groups and namespaces
examples.description: A namespace is a path that helps locate a GitLab project. Groups and subgroups can add levels to that path.
examples.code:
Example path: school-club/web/reading-list
Top group: school-club
Subgroup: web
Project: reading-list

examples.title: Use labels to organise issues
examples.description: Labels mark kinds of work so issues can be filtered or grouped. A label should have a meaning the team understands.
examples.code:
Issue: Search misses lowercase titles
Labels: bug, search
Meaning of bug: current behaviour differs from the intended behaviour

examples.title: Plan related work with milestones
examples.description: A milestone groups issues and merge requests around a goal or period. It helps show what work remains for that goal.
examples.code:
Milestone: Reading-list first demo
Issue 1: show sample books
Issue 2: add a search box
Issue 3: check keyboard use

examples.title: Make an issue board useful
examples.description: An issue board shows work in columns based on chosen project rules, often using labels. It helps a team see items waiting or in progress.
examples.code:
Board labels: ready, doing, review
Card: Add empty-state text
Current label: doing
Next condition: move to review when the change and checks are ready

examples.title: Prepare a merge request
examples.description: A merge request, or MR, proposes combining a source branch into a target branch. It connects code changes with review and pipeline results.
examples.code:
Source branch: improve-empty-state
Target branch: main
Change: show No books found when search has no matches
Check: search for a title that is absent

examples.title: Resolve review discussions
examples.description: Review discussions can point to a specific line or behaviour. Resolving one should mean the concern has been addressed or an agreed decision has been recorded.
examples.code:
Reviewer: what should appear for a query containing only spaces?
Author: treat it as an empty query
Change: trim the query before filtering
Check: add the spaces-only case

examples.title: Read a CI pipeline file
examples.description: GitLab CI/CD reads jobs from its pipeline configuration. A job names commands for a runner, which is the worker that executes them.
examples.code:
File: .gitlab-ci.yml
Job name: test
Stage: test
Script: npm test

examples.title: Understand stages and jobs
examples.description: Stages can group pipeline jobs in an order such as build then test. Jobs in one stage may run in parallel when runners are available.
examples.code:
Stage 1: build
  Job: create app files
Stage 2: test
  Job: unit checks
  Job: accessibility checks

examples.title: Keep useful job artifacts
examples.description: An artifact is a saved file from a job, such as a test report or built package. It lets later steps or reviewers inspect useful results.
examples.code:
Job: accessibility checks
Artifact: accessibility-report.json
Purpose: inspect which pages passed or failed
Retention: keep only as long as the project needs

examples.title: Use protected branches and merge checks
examples.description: A protected branch restricts who can push or merge. Merge checks can require useful conditions, such as a successful pipeline, before combining code.
examples.code:
Plan for main:
Restrict direct pushes
Use merge requests
Require the agreed pipeline result
Review open discussions and required approvals

examples.title: Read an environment status honestly
examples.description: An environment represents a place where an application runs, such as a preview or production site. A deployment record links a version to that place.
examples.code:
Environment: preview
Deployment: commit abc123 from the example project
Checks: page loads and search works
Limit: this status does not describe production
